spans.s:
Naicā-śākha is found in one passage of the Rigveda, where Sāyaṇa renders it as ‘of low origin,’ but elsewhere he explains it as the name of a place. The former sense is accepted by Grassmann and Ludwig in their versions, and by Zimmer, but Hillebrandt points out that the reference is rather to the ‘low-branched’ soma plant. Cf. kīkaṭa and pramaganda.
Foot notes vii. 53, 4.
See St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
Altindisches Leben, 31.
Vedische Mythologie, 1, 14-18; 2, 241245, where he opposes Bo7htlingk's view that it is a proper name.

Naicu-dāra occurs in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, meaning ‘composed of the wood of the Nicudāra.’ What tree is meant by the latter name is unknown.
Foot notes xxi. 4, 13. Cf. Anupada sūtra, vi. 4.
